principles: Only fix the misleading status rendering, not resolver policy.
Host-neutral output must report configured facts without making host choices.
Fail-closed unresolved layouts must remain visibly unresolved.
Regression tests must exercise user-visible CLI output.
drivers: Users currently see Non-git project even after configured-git-root resolution succeeds.
The real correctness issue is mismatch between signed workspace state and host/status presentation.
B-526c already added explicit repair; this story should consume that state rather than invent a second repair path.

options.name: A: Add session_brief display logic for configured gitRoot resolution
pros: Smallest fix to the actual user-visible mismatch
Keeps automatic repair out of session_brief
cons: Adds another status block to session_brief output

options.name: B: Change isGitRepository to treat configured gitRoot as git-ready
pros: Would suppress the old warning with less rendering code
cons: Conflates metadata root git status with signed workspace status
Could mislead worktree/bootstrap guidance and hide unresolved states

options.name: C: Auto-run config repair from session_brief when one child repo exists
pros: Would make future users avoid a manual command
cons: Mutates config from a read-only command
Optimizes arbitrarily instead of fixing presentation correctness

chosen: A: Add session_brief display logic for configured gitRoot resolution
rationale: Choose A because the bug is a display mismatch: configured gitRoot resolution is already authoritative, so session_brief should show it without changing resolver or mutating config.

preMortem.scenario: session_brief claims OK for a non-git metadata root with invalid gitRoot
preMortem.trigger: display code trusts config.gitRoot text without verifying resolver output
preMortem.consequence: review_run_start can still fail while Host says OK
preMortem.mitigation: Only show signed workspace OK after story signed workspace resolver returns resolved configured-git-root or equivalent verified state.

preMortem.scenario: unresolved wrapper roots lose their fail-closed warning
preMortem.trigger: new branch suppresses Non-git project warning whenever a child repo exists
preMortem.consequence: users think Lattice will choose a repo automatically
preMortem.mitigation: Do not scan or choose child repos in session_brief; unresolved projects keep explicit non-git/unresolved guidance.

preMortem.scenario: status output becomes too noisy on normal git projects
preMortem.trigger: new block renders for all projects rather than non-git configured wrapper roots
preMortem.mitigation: Render the new configured-gitRoot block only when metadata root is non-git and configured gitRoot resolution is available or configured but invalid.
